hero.badge: For research, strategy, and knowledge teams · Runs locally
hero.title: A local AI workbench for research and due diligence
hero.subtitle:
Privix helps investment, strategy, and knowledge teams organize materials, run multi-Agent research, and produce auditable reports on their own machines.
Documents, data, and API keys stay local.

stats.research_label: Break questions into multi-Agent tasks for retrieval, analysis, and synthesis
stats.diligence_label: Move leads, companies, files, scoring, and approvals in one local workbench
stats.knowledge_label: Turn local documents into a reusable knowledge base your Agents can query
stats.control_label: Model calls, Agent actions, and key config changes leave local records

enterprise.title: Control for research-heavy teams
enterprise.subtitle: When materials are sensitive, workflows are complex, and outputs need review, Privix lets teams start using AI locally first.
enterprise.card1_desc: All conversations, documents, and research artifacts are stored in a local SQLite. No upload, no sync, no cloud replica. Compliance, legal, and internal audit teams can inspect directly.
enterprise.card2_desc: Model credentials are stored in the OS keychain. Privix does not relay or proxy traffic and holds no keys. Switch providers at any time.
enterprise.card3_desc: Every Agent call and model request writes to a local log. Database, configuration, and log paths are fully open.
enterprise.card4_desc: 10 MB installer, desktop-grade deployment. IT does not need to provision a server, gateway, or container cluster — employees install and run locally.
enterprise.cta_desc: Need rollout support, private-deployment customization, or an NDA?

enterpriseEdition.title: Privix Enterprise — Multi-tenant for Organizations
enterpriseEdition.subtitle: When HR / IT / compliance need to govern every employee's Agent, desktop-local isn't enough. Enterprise layers tenant management on top: centralized keys, unified audit, cost quotas, SSO login.
enterpriseEdition.card1_desc: Organization / user / role three-level isolation via Postgres RLS. Keycloak OIDC integrated — users sign in via WeCom / Feishu / Okta and are auto-provisioned by group.
enterpriseEdition.card2_desc: Admins configure OpenAI / Anthropic / Gemini / Azure / DeepSeek / Qwen / Ollama keys once; all tenant members use them. AES-256-GCM at rest, plaintext never returned.
enterpriseEdition.card3_desc: All completions route through the server gateway with streaming SSE passthrough. Per-tenant tokens / cost recorded, monthly USD / call caps enforceable (429 on breach).
enterpriseEdition.card4_desc: Login / key rotation / Agent calls / quota edits fully audited in Postgres. Helm Chart + Docker Compose bring up the full stack (Postgres + Redis + Keycloak + server + admin).
enterpriseEdition.cta_desc: Interested in being an early pilot? Book a demo, tech preview, or private-deployment assessment.

features.title: Three teams, three clearer workflows
features.subtitle: Start from the job you need to finish, then open the Invest, Knowledge, or SOP module as needed.
features.row1_title: Investment teams: from lead to diligence report
features.row1_desc: Keep deal pools, company profiles, pitch decks, initial reviews, scoring, and approvals in one local workbench. AI helps with research and material prep; humans keep judgment and ownership.
features.row2_title: Knowledge teams: turn materials into a queryable KB
features.row2_desc: Turn PDFs, Word docs, Markdown, and project records into a local knowledge layer Agents can search and reuse. Built for internal archives, research files, and team Q&A.
features.row3_desc: Represent rules, roles, tools, and steps as structured workflows Agents can execute. Useful for fixed-format documents, approval packets, retrospectives, and repeatable research tasks.

ai.title: From materials to reports, keep research work local
ai.subtitle: Privix is not another chat window. It brings files, models, Agents, workflows, and audit trails into one local workbench.
ai.assistant_title: When something breaks, the built-in assistant helps locate it
ai.assistant_desc: No guessing whether the model, Gateway, Agent, or Skills layer failed. Claw Doctor checks the environment, reads logs, diagnoses connection issues, and records repair actions locally.
ai.fleet_title: Manage models, tools, and local Agents in one place
ai.fleet_desc: Stop reconfiguring the same tools across separate apps. Privix detects Claude Code, Codex, Gemini, Qwen, and other CLI Agents, manages 23 LLM providers and MCP tools, and keeps team configuration on the machine.
ai.evo_title: Turn open-ended questions into research reports
ai.evo_desc: Give Privix a research goal and it decomposes the work across multiple Scientist Agents, collecting evidence, conclusions, and a structured report. Good for competitor analysis, market sizing, technical evaluation, and investment screening.
ai.swarm_title: Coordinate multiple Agents along a task chain
ai.swarm_desc: Break due diligence, document review, or competitor monitoring into a DAG task chain. Agents execute in waves and consolidate a traceable result. You can adjust roles, dependencies, or start from built-in templates.
ai.hermes_desc: OpenClaw handles multi-Agent orchestration and tool chains; Hermes handles streaming chat and Python ecosystem integration. Switch by scenario while keeping configuration, services, and logs isolated.

tutorials.title: Run one real workflow first
tutorials.subtitle: If you only want to understand what Privix does, start with either investment diligence or local Agent setup.
tutorials.invest_title: Run an investment diligence flow in 10 minutes
tutorials.invest_desc: From lead and company profile to document archive and approval, see Privix as a full workbench rather than a single chat UI.
tutorials.invest_s1_desc: Populate the dashboard with sample tasks and records so you can explore the full deal pipeline.
tutorials.invest_s2_desc: Enter a project name, industry and owner into the deal pool to get your first lead into the system.
tutorials.invest_s3_desc: Promote a promising project to a Deal and experience stage progression and to-do tracking.
tutorials.invest_s4_desc: Upload review materials to the document library so Deals and SOPs work from the same source.
tutorials.invest_s5_desc: Once materials are ready, push to approval and let the system handle reminders and decision logging.
tutorials.agent_title: Configure your first working local Agent
tutorials.agent_desc: Wire models, Gateway, Agent, and Skills together so your local AI can actually start working.
tutorials.agent_s1_desc: Verify Node.js, OpenClaw CLI and config files are in place before proceeding.
tutorials.agent_s2_desc: Add at least one primary model so your Agent has reasoning capability.
tutorials.agent_s3_desc: Spin up your first Agent with its own identity, model and workspace.
tutorials.agent_s4_title: Feed Skills or Import a Persona
tutorials.agent_s4_desc: Confirm available Skills, or import a persona config from the AI Assistant page to personalize your Agent.
tutorials.agent_s5_desc: Send your first message in live chat and confirm the Agent responds correctly.

privacy.title: Sensitive research should not start in someone else's cloud
privacy.subtitle: Privix keeps documents, conversations, model keys, and audit logs local. Only when you invoke a model does your machine call the provider you configured.
privacy.card1_desc: Research materials, project records, sessions, and Agent configuration are stored in a local SQLite file, with no forced sync or cloud replica.
privacy.card2_title: API keys are not handed to Privix
privacy.card2_desc: Model keys are encrypted in the OS keychain. Privix does not custody keys or proxy requests; calls go directly to your configured provider.
privacy.card3_desc: When you are not invoking a model, you can still browse archives, edit projects, maintain SOPs, and organize knowledge bases. Network access is for model calls, not data storage.
privacy.card4_desc: Agent calls, model requests, and configuration changes write to local logs for review, audit, and troubleshooting.

tech.title: Under the hood, for teams that need to verify
tech.subtitle: Privix is a desktop-grade local workbench: Rust backend, SQLite local storage, and dual Agent engines with OpenClaw and Hermes.
tech.tauri_desc: Rust backend + system WebView. ~10 MB installer, no Electron runtime required. Cross-platform: macOS, Windows, Linux.
tech.vite_desc: Zero framework dependencies. Millisecond HMR with Vite, native CSS variable-driven theming.
tech.sqlite_desc: Projects, sessions, and Agent configurations are all stored in a local SQLite file. No cloud replica, no forced sync. Deletion is irreversible.
tech.openclaw_desc: OpenClaw handles multi-agent orchestration and MCP tool chains; Hermes provides SSE streaming chat and Python ecosystem integration. 23 LLM providers out of the box, switch engines per scenario.

docs.title: Not sure where to start? Pick by background
docs.subtitle: New users can install first, technical users can configure Agents directly, and teams can hand structured product knowledge to an AI assistant.
docs.beginner_desc: No coding needed. Follow 8 steps, 30 minutes from download to chatting. Built-in AI assistant helps if you get stuck.
docs.usage_desc: 6 steps to a fully working setup, plus troubleshooting checklist, daily ops tips, and a 9-concept glossary. For users with some tech background.
docs.agent_desc: Copy the full text and feed it to any AI. Product architecture, troubleshooting decision trees, and full FAQ — lets Claw Doctor or ChatGPT answer Privix questions.

beginner.title: Start from Zero, We'll Walk You Through
beginner.subtitle: No coding needed. No command line required. Follow these 8 steps and you'll have Privix running in 30 minutes.
beginner.qb1_text: None. If you can install apps, you're good.
beginner.qb2_text: About 30 min, depends on internet speed.
beginner.qb3_text: Ask the built-in AI assistant, or send a screenshot to ChatGPT.
beginner.editions_title: Three Industry Modules — Enter What You Need
beginner.editions_subtitle: Privix is now a single app. Invest / Knowledge / SOP are enabled as industry modules, so you no longer need separate installers.
beginner.v128_desc: Privix now ships as one app; Invest / Knowledge / SOP are enabled as modules. SkillHub, chat stability, and the dual-engine setup are already part of the current release.
beginner.steps_subtitle: After each step, check the "How to know it worked" section before moving on.
beginner.s1_p1: Mac or Windows, as long as it's connected to the internet. Phones and tablets won't work — it has to be a computer.
beginner.s1_p2: You don't need to know programming or what a "command line" is. If we need you to type a command later, we'll spell it out word by word.
beginner.s1_p3: Having a tech-savvy colleague helps, but it's not required. The app has a built-in AI assistant that can help.
beginner.s1_check: You have a computer with internet access. That's it.
beginner.s2_title: Just Like Installing Any Other App
beginner.s2_p1: Go to the download page and grab the installer.
beginner.s2_mac_p1: Download the .dmg file, double-click it, drag the icon into the Applications folder. Done.
beginner.s2_mac_p2: The first time you open it, macOS will probably warn you about an "unverified developer" or say it's "damaged". It's not a virus, don't worry. Fix: Apple menu → System Settings → Privacy & Security → find the Privix block → click "Open Anyway".
beginner.s2_win_p1: Download the .exe file, double-click, click "Next" all the way through. If there's a security warning, choose "Run anyway".
beginner.s2_check: You can find Privix on your desktop or app list, and it opens when you double-click.
beginner.s3_p1: The first launch will take you to the "Initial Setup" page. It automatically checks if your computer has everything it needs.
beginner.s3_p2: A green check means it's fine. A red X means something's missing — don't worry, follow the instructions below.
beginner.s3_nodejs_p: Node.js is a tool — you don't need to know what it does, just install it. Open your browser, go to "nodejs.org", download and install. Then come back and refresh.
beginner.s3_openclaw_p: Just click the "Install" button on the page and wait a few minutes. It'll install itself.
beginner.s3_terminal_p: It's a text window where you type commands. On Mac, press Command+Space, search "Terminal" and hit Enter. On Windows, press the Win key, search "cmd" and hit Enter. But normally you won't need it — the buttons on the page do the job.
beginner.s3_check: All check items are green. Got a red item you can't fix? Skip it for now, set up the AI assistant in Step 4, and let it help you.
beginner.s4_meta: Set Up Claw Doctor (Your AI Helper)
beginner.s4_p1: Find "Claw Doctor" in the left menu and click it. This is the app's built-in AI assistant — you can ask it anything when you get stuck later.
beginner.s4_p2: But it can't work yet — you need to give it an AI model (like installing a brain for it).
beginner.s4_step1: Click the "Settings" button in the top right
beginner.s4_step2: Fill in the AI model info. You'll need an API Key (basically a password)
beginner.s4_step3: Not sure what to use? Try MiniMax (has free credits), or ask a tech colleague for an API Key
beginner.s4_step4: After filling in, click "Test Connection" — if it says success, you're done
beginner.s4_check: Type "hello" in Claw Doctor and it replies. From now on, ask it whenever you have questions.
beginner.s4_callout_desc: From this point on, whenever you're stuck, just describe your problem in Claw Doctor. It's your personal tech support — no waiting in line.
beginner.s5_title: Fire Up the Main Engine Too
beginner.s5_p1: What you just configured was the assistant's own model. Now you need to set up the main system engine so live chat, Agents and other features can work.
beginner.s5_step1: Find "Model Configuration" in the left menu, add an AI model (can be the same one as Claw Doctor)
beginner.s5_step3: Then go to the "Dashboard" or "Service Management" page
beginner.s5_step5: Wait until it turns green and shows "Running"
beginner.s5_check: Model test passed, Gateway shows green "Running". Won't start? Ask Claw Doctor.
beginner.s6_p1: Find "Live Chat" in the left menu, click in, and type anything — like "Hello, tell me about yourself".
beginner.s6_p2: Got a reply? Congrats, the system is up and running!
beginner.s6_p3: No reply? Check if Gateway is still "Running". If it's green but not responding, tell Claw Doctor "Live chat sent a message but got no reply" and it'll investigate.
beginner.s6_check: Sent a message and got a reply. Core features are working.
beginner.s7_title: It's Working — See What Else Is in Here
beginner.s7_p1: The basics are running. Check these out as you wish — no need to try everything:
beginner.s7_ai1: SkillHub — where you install new Agent skills, find it in the Skills page
beginner.s7_ai2: Prospect-Research Scientist Cluster — multiple AIs collaborate on complex tasks, 12 ready-made templates
beginner.s7_ai3: Agentic Swarm — give a goal, AI breaks it into tasks and agents work in parallel
beginner.s7_wiki1: Karpathy-style Wiki — drop in PDFs / Word / Markdown, the AI reads them and splits output into entity, concept, and synthesis pages with [[cross-link]] references — a living wiki
beginner.s7_wiki2: Ingest / Query / Lint in one flow — import new material with diff preview, ask questions and get citation-backed answers, auto-repair broken structure
beginner.s7_wiki3: Open any knowledge base from the Knowledge page → switch to the Wiki tab
beginner.s7_invest: Investment workflows (when the Invest module is enabled)
beginner.s7_invest1: Investment Dashboard — bird's eye view of your deal pool
beginner.s7_invest2: Deal Pipeline — kanban board from sourcing to closing
beginner.s7_invest3: Company DB + Contacts — manage companies and people
beginner.s7_channel_p: Feishu/Lark: Setup is complex, consider getting help from a tech colleague. Telegram: Simplest option, takes just a few minutes.
beginner.s7_check: You have a general idea of what's in the system and tried a few things that interested you.
beginner.s8_m1: Ask Claw Doctor first. Just describe your problem, like "Gateway is still red, what do I do?" — it usually has the answer.
beginner.s8_m2: Ask an external AI. Send a screenshot or this web page link to ChatGPT / Claude and say "I'm using Privix and ran into this issue".
beginner.s8_m3: Check the Advanced Guide. The Advanced Guide has detailed manuals and troubleshooting checklists.
beginner.s8_tip: One more thing: don't reinstall at the first sign of trouble. Most issues have simple fixes. Reinstalling might actually lose your configuration. Ask AI first.
beginner.s8_check: You know who to ask when something goes wrong.
beginner.faq1_desc: That's macOS security, not actual damage. Go to System Settings → Privacy & Security → find Privix → click "Open Anyway". See Step 2 for details.
beginner.faq2_title: Opened the app and see a bunch of red
beginner.faq2_desc: Red means something's missing. Follow the on-screen instructions to install. If stuck, tell Claw Doctor "XX is red in initial setup" and it'll guide you.
beginner.faq3_title: Clicked Start but Gateway is still red
beginner.faq3_desc: Most likely the model isn't configured properly, or the port is occupied by another program. Tell Claw Doctor "Gateway won't start" and let it diagnose.
beginner.faq4_title: Sent a message but nobody replied
beginner.faq4_desc: Check the Dashboard — is Gateway showing green "Running"? If not, start it first. If it's green and still no reply, ask Claw Doctor to investigate.
beginner.final_title: Done? Check Out the Advanced Guide
beginner.final_desc: The beginner guide got you up and running. To learn how each feature works in detail, check the advanced guide.

usage.title: Privix Advanced Usage Guide
usage.subtitle:
You probably know what a command line is and have used plenty of software — just not Privix yet.
6 steps to get the system running, plus daily ops tips, troubleshooting checklist and glossary.
Total beginner? See the Beginner Guide. Need structured docs for AI? See Agent Knowledge Base.
usage.qb2_text: Full setup from install to Agent going live
usage.steps_subtitle: Ordered by real usage flow. Each step explains what, why, and how to know you're done.
usage.order_title: Install → Claw Doctor → Models & Gateway → Agent + Skills → Live Chat Test → Connect Channels
usage.order_desc: Why configure Claw Doctor first? Because if anything goes wrong later, you can just ask it. Like finding the medic before heading into battle.
usage.outline_title: These 6 Steps Will Get You Through
usage.outline2: Set up Claw Doctor as your troubleshooter
usage.outline4: Create an Agent and attach Skills
usage.outline5: Verify the full chain via live chat
usage.s1_title: After Installing, Run Through Initial Setup
usage.s1_p1: After installation, the first launch takes you to "Initial Setup". Don't skip it — check every item. These are the foundation for everything else.
usage.s1_b1: macOS blocked on first open: drag to Applications, System Settings → Privacy & Security → Open Anyway.
usage.s1_b2: Windows OpenClaw install error: check admin permissions, npm cache, and Git HTTPS config.
usage.s1_b3: Linux without desktop: use Web deployment — panel on :1420, Gateway on :18789.
usage.s1_check: Initial Setup shows Node.js, Git, OpenClaw, and config file all passed.
usage.s1_desktop_p: Mac / Windows users: download, install, first launch goes straight to Initial Setup.
usage.s1_web_p: Linux / server scenarios. Default :1420 panel, :18789 Gateway.
usage.s2_title: Get Something That Can Help You Debug
usage.s2_p1: Claw Doctor is not the same as the OpenClaw Agent you'll build later. It's a built-in standalone AI assistant for troubleshooting, Q&A, and log analysis.
usage.s2_b1: Go to the "Claw Doctor" page and configure its model.
usage.s2_b2: Even before your Agent is ready, you already have a helper that can read errors and suggest fixes.
usage.s2_b3: Model issues, Gateway crashes, missing Skill dependencies — just toss them to the assistant.
usage.s2_check: Claw Doctor can chat normally. Your "tech support" is on duty.
usage.tools_desc: Common tasks don't need lengthy descriptions — just tap a card. Not sure which? Start with "Check System Environment" and "One-Click Diagnostics".
usage.tool1_desc: Reads openclaw.json and checks providers, Gateway settings, and common config mistakes.
usage.tool1_tip: When to use: just installed, just changed config, suspect something's wrong
usage.tool2_desc: Checks process, ports and logs to determine if Gateway isn't started, isn't listening, or is in a bad state.
usage.tool2_tip: When to use: chat won't connect, port errors, Gateway acting up
usage.tool3_desc: Checks Node.js, npm, OpenClaw CLI and port status to confirm the base environment is intact.
usage.tool3_tip: When to use: install stuck, things broke after upgrade
usage.tool4_desc: Runs a full checkup across config, models, Gateway, WebSocket, and Node.js.
usage.tool4_tip: When to use: something suddenly stopped working, don't know where to start
usage.tool5_desc: Searches logs for ERROR, WARN, fail keywords to narrow down the problem.
usage.tool5_tip: When to use: you see errors but can't understand them
usage.tool6_desc: Shows which Skills work, which are missing dependencies, and guides you to fix them.
usage.tool6_tip: When to use: Agent can chat but won't use tools
usage.s3_title: Models Control the Brains, Gateway Is the Main Switch
usage.s3_p1: "Model Configuration" sets which AI model OpenClaw uses. "Service Management" controls whether Gateway is running. Both need to be working for the system to come alive.
usage.s3_b1: Configure at least 1 primary model. Better to add 1-2 backups so if the main one goes down, there's a fallback.
usage.s3_b2: Save after model test passes. If you changed config, you may need to restart Gateway for changes to take effect.
usage.s3_b3: Go to "Service Management" and confirm Gateway shows green Running. If not, check the logs.
usage.s3_callout_title: Current builds make Gateway more stable
usage.s3_callout_desc: Current builds already include a steadier Gateway watchdog strategy: throttled refresh, auto-retry on dropped connections, and a short buffer before restart to avoid flapping.
usage.s3_check: Primary model test passed, Gateway shows green Running.
usage.s4_title: Start Simple — Don't Overload It Right Away
usage.s4_p1: Go to "Agent Management" and create your first Agent. Give it a clear name, define its role, pick a model, and get it running first.
usage.s4_b1: First Agent should do just one thing. Don't stuff all capabilities into it.
usage.s4_b2: Agent ID: all lowercase, short and memorable. Display name: whatever you like.
usage.s4_b3: Model controls how smart it is, Skills control what it can do, identity files control who it acts like.
usage.s4_callout_title: Current builds include the SkillHub store
usage.s4_callout_desc: Skills page now has a "Store" tab. Browse skills online, click to install — no command line needed. Different Agents can have separate Skills directories.
usage.s4_check: Your Agent list has one Agent you created, with at least one key Skill showing as available.
usage.s4_pitfall_p: "I can see Skills on the page so they must be working" — not necessarily. Check if the status shows "Available".
usage.s4_advice_p: Make sure 1-2 core capabilities actually work before adding more.
usage.s5_title: Send a Message — See If It Actually Responds
usage.s5_p1: Go to "Live Chat" and send a message. Everything you configured might "look fine" on their own pages, but only a response here proves the whole chain works.
usage.s5_p2: A response means: Gateway is running, model is callable, Agent loaded successfully, permissions aren't blocking.
usage.s5_callout_title: Current builds provide richer chat status
usage.s5_callout_desc: You can now see what the Agent is doing — thinking, planning, waiting for approval. A timer shows at the bottom after sending, and if there's no response after 3 minutes, you'll get a timeout notification. No more silent message drops.
usage.s5_test_msg: Hello, in three sentences tell me who you are, what you can do, and which model you're currently using.
usage.s5_check: Got a reply from the Agent. Officially upgraded from "installed" to "working".
usage.s6_title: Want Your Agent on Feishu or Telegram?
usage.s6_p1: The "Messaging Channels" page manages all external connections. Regardless of platform, two prerequisites are the same: Gateway must be running, and you need to publish/approve on the platform side after saving.
usage.s6_b1: Feishu / Lark: Create a custom enterprise app on Feishu Open Platform, enable bot capability, get App ID and App Secret. Recommend WebSocket for event subscription. After saving, you still need to publish the app version on Feishu.
usage.s6_b2: Telegram: Create a Bot via @BotFather, get the Token, prepare allowed user IDs, fill in and save. Simplest external channel.
usage.s6_b3: Saved but not working? Check if Gateway is running, if the platform app is published, and if the bot has been added to the group.
usage.s6_check: The bot can receive and reply to messages on Feishu or Telegram.
usage.s6_feishu_p: Needs App ID and App Secret. Supports built-in and official plugin modes. Bot visible to others only after app version is published.
usage.s6_tg_p: Needs Bot Token and user IDs. Lightest option, best for quickly getting your first external channel working.
usage.s7_title: Let Your KB Grow Its Own Living Wiki
usage.s7_p1: v1.6.0 adds a Karpathy-style Wiki — a structured knowledge layer for your Agents. Drop in PDFs / Word / Markdown and the AI splits them into three page types (entity / concept / synthesis), maintaining [[cross-link]] references, an index, and a log. Unlike chunk-and-embed retrieval, here the LLM hand-maintains structured content.
usage.s7_flow1: Go to the Knowledge page → open a KB → switch to the Wiki tab → the first visit initializes the SCHEMA.md / index.md / log.md / pages/ skeleton
usage.s7_flow2: Ingest: pick a source file and hit "Propose Ingest" — the system sends it to Hermes (falls back to manual paste if Hermes is unavailable) and returns a set of .md pages to write, with a diff preview for selective apply
usage.s7_flow3: Query: type a question at the top of the Wiki tab — the LLM reads the index, pulls the relevant pages, synthesizes a citation-backed answer, and optionally persists it as a synthesis page
usage.s7_flow4: Lint: one pass flags broken [[links]], orphan pages, and pages that don't match SCHEMA, with repair suggestions
usage.s7_flow5: Obsidian export: the Wiki layout is Obsidian-vault compatible — one click exports to your local vault for continued editing
usage.s7_callout_desc: Best for knowledge that accumulates over time in a single domain — research libraries, regulatory KBs, product knowledge. Not worth it for one-shot Q&A (chat alone is enough). Wiki's value: next time you ask, the LLM sees its own prior structured concept pages instead of raw fragments.
usage.s7_check: You can see the file tree in the Wiki tab, successfully ingested at least one source file, and applied its diff.
usage.habit_desc: After each step, if you're not sure you're done, just ask Claw Doctor: "I just configured models, what should I do next?" Way faster than searching around the UI.
usage.daily_title: Daily Usage: Keep an Eye on These 4 Things
usage.daily_subtitle: Once you're comfortable, what saves time isn't "knowing how to configure" but "knowing where to look".
usage.daily1_desc: Agent suddenly not responding? 9 times out of 10, the model dropped. Check API Key, Base URL, primary model connectivity. If you have a backup model, see if it can take over.
usage.daily2_desc: Personal use? Set to "localhost only". Sharing? Configure Token or password. Don't change security settings without reason.
usage.daily3_desc: Name and role clearly defined, backup before major changes, one Agent per task type. When something breaks, you'll immediately know which one to fix.
usage.daily4_title: Check Logs Before Asking for Help
usage.daily4_desc: Don't rush to reinstall. First check live chat behavior, then logs, then run diagnostics. Only escalate to Claw Doctor when you've truly hit a wall.
usage.daily_pages_desc: Claw Doctor: ask questions, troubleshoot. Service Management: start/stop Gateway, backup config. Log Viewer: Gateway and error logs. Memory Files: Agent work memory. About: check current version.
usage.fix_subtitle: Most common issues, organized by symptom.
usage.fix1_b1: Is live chat connected to Gateway?
usage.fix1_b2: Does the primary model pass the test in Model Configuration?
usage.fix1_b3: Is the Agent bound to a model?
usage.fix1_b4: Is Gateway auth blocking the request?
usage.fix1_b5: Send the specific error to Claw Doctor and let it determine which layer is failing.
usage.fix2_title: Can Chat but Won't Use Skills
usage.fix2_b1: Is the corresponding Skill showing "Available" on the Skills page?
usage.fix2_b2: Missing command-line tools or environment variables?
usage.fix2_b3: Are Gateway tool permissions set too strict?
usage.fix2_b4: Do Agent rules lock out certain capabilities?
usage.fix2_b5: Screenshot the status and send to Claw Doctor — it can usually tell you exactly what's missing.
usage.fix3_b1: Did you recently switch OpenClaw versions?
usage.fix3_b2: Is the current version higher than the recommended stable version?
usage.fix3_b3: Did you recently change providers, tokens, or security settings?
usage.fix3_b4: Figure out what changed first, then fix.
usage.fix3_b5: Screenshot or copy logs to Claw Doctor.
usage.fix4_b1: Don't delete the Agent or reinstall.
usage.fix4_b2: Think about three things: what it could do before, what's wrong now, what you changed recently.
usage.fix4_b3: Toss those three answers to Claw Doctor.
usage.fix4_b4: Check in this order: environment → models → Gateway → Skills → the Agent itself.
usage.rescue_msg: My OpenClaw Agent in Privix used to reply normally but now it doesn't. Please check each layer — environment, models, Gateway, Skills, Agent config — and tell me the most likely cause and which page to check first.
usage.glossary_subtitle: After reading these, you won't get lost in the jargon.
usage.g1_desc: Privix is the app interface (the cockpit). OpenClaw and Hermes are the dual engines running behind it. OpenClaw handles multi-agent orchestration; Hermes provides streaming chat. You can use one or both.
usage.g2_desc: Think of it as the central dispatcher. Chat messages, model calls, Agent actions — everything goes through it. If Gateway's not running, nothing works.
usage.g3_desc: An Agent is a "character". It has its own name, model, rules, memory, and skill scope. Creating an Agent = creating a new role.
usage.g4_desc: A plugin that determines what an Agent can do besides chatting. Some Skills require additional command-line tools or environment variables.
usage.g5_desc: The built-in skill store in current Privix releases. You can now search and install Skills directly in the UI instead of relying on command-line setup.
usage.g6_desc: Claw Doctor is a built-in troubleshooting tool. Agents are the AI characters you create and train. One is tech support, the other is your employee.
usage.g7_desc: One model works fine — until it doesn't. AI services occasionally have outages. With a backup, when the primary goes down, it auto-switches and your Agent keeps working.
usage.g8_desc: An Agent's "desk". Identity files, behavior rules, memory files, task materials — all stored here. Think of it as the employee's folder.
usage.g9_title: Should You Chase the Latest Version
usage.g9_desc: No. Stick with the recommended stable version. Upgrading too aggressively might introduce compatibility issues that take more time to fix than they save.
usage.final_title: All Set — Time to Get to Work
usage.final_desc: The full chain is running. Need structured docs for AI? Check the Agent Knowledge Base. Want to explore more features? Head back to the homepage.

agent.subtitle: This document is for AIs to read. Copy the full text below and feed it to Claw Doctor, ChatGPT, Claude, or any AI platform that supports knowledge bases — it'll then be able to answer questions about Privix.
agent.howto_title: How to Use This Knowledge Base
agent.howto_desc: Copy all the content above and paste it into whatever AI you're using. Could be Claw Doctor's built-in knowledge, ChatGPT's custom instructions, Claude's project knowledge, or any platform that supports knowledge base imports. Recommend re-copying after version updates.
agent.final_title: Copied? Go Feed It to Your AI
agent.final_desc: Paste it into Claw Doctor, ChatGPT, Claude, or any AI platform. Want to set things up yourself? Check the beginner or advanced guide.
